questions.explain: The five AI-required capabilities are curated feature storage, vector storage and similarity search, sanctioned model execution paths, input quality gates, and model lifecycle management — implemented as DBA-owned patterns on the existing SQL Server estate.
options: Bigger hardware and a new database engine
A data lake and a separate vector database
Curated feature storage, vector storage, sanctioned model execution, input quality gates, and model lifecycle management
Replacing all stored procedures with Python microservices
questions.q: According to the chapter, what five capabilities make a SQL Server platform AI-ready?

questions.explain: Point-in-time correctness stamps every feature row with the as-of date its inputs were valid for, making training-serving skew — accidentally training on information from the future — structurally impossible.
options: Storing features in the same tables as production transactions
Stamping every feature row with the as-of date its inputs were valid for, preventing training-serving skew
Recomputing all features from scratch before every training run
Keeping only the latest feature values with no history
questions.q: What does point-in-time correctness mean in the feature store design, and why does it matter?

questions.explain: The DBA decisions for vector search are lifecycle and governance — re-embedding policy on source change, dimension discipline enforced by the VECTOR(n) declaration, and RLS scoping by tenant — not the choice of embedding model.
options: Choosing the embedding model and tuning its hyperparameters
Writing the vector distance functions from scratch
Lifecycle and governance: re-embedding policy, dimension discipline, and RLS scoping by tenant
Deciding which programming language the data scientists use
questions.q: For vector storage and semantic search in SQL Server, which decisions does the chapter assign to the DBA?

questions.explain: A halted pipeline pages someone today; a poisoned feature store silently degrades every model trained on it for months, so the gate THROWs loudly instead of letting bad features through.
options: A halted pipeline pages someone today, while a poisoned feature store silently degrades models for months
THROW is required by the SQL Server license agreement
Quality gates only work when they fail the batch
Logging check results is optional
questions.q: Why does the feature quality gate use THROW to halt the pipeline on a failed check instead of just logging a warning?

questions.explain: The registry records model version, feature version trained on, training cutoff, and status; when predictions degrade, that lineage reveals whether the model, the features, or the world changed — each pointing at a different fix.
options: To satisfy a naming convention for model files
To track which data scientist trained each model for performance reviews
To store ONNX binaries because the file system is unreliable
To record model version, feature version, and training cutoff so prediction degradation can be traced to its cause
questions.q: What is the purpose of the ml.model_registry table's lineage columns (feature_version, training_cutoff)?
